findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'WeakDerivStep'` over `code/` yields hits for `WeakDerivStep.*` only inside GraphStep.lean; W2p.lean and W3p.lean reference only `WeakDerivStepJetLp` (W2p:64, W3p:64), `weakDerivStepSubmodule` (W2p:70, W3p:70) and `mem_weakDerivStepSubmodule_iff{,_hasWeakFDerivOn}` (W2p:79,88; W3p:80,88).
findings.fix: Define the order-specific projections as the step's, e.g. `def W2p.firstOrderL := WeakDerivStep.prevL W1p.gradientL`, `def W2p.hessianL := WeakDerivStep.derivL W1p.gradientL`, `def W3p.secondOrderL := WeakDerivStep.prevL W2p.hessianL`, `def W3p.thirdDerivativeL := WeakDerivStep.derivL W2p.hessianL`, and reduce each order-specific lemma to a one-line application of the corresponding `WeakDerivStep` lemma. If the specialized names are meant to be the only API, delete lines 192-290 instead.
findings.issue: The `WeakDerivStep` namespace (lines 192-290: `prevL`, `prev`, `prevL_apply`, `prev_coe`, `derivL`, `deriv`, `derivL_apply`, `deriv_coe`, `mk`, `prev_mk`, `deriv_mk`, `hasWeakFDerivOn_prev`, `norm_prev_le`, `norm_deriv_le`, `norm_sq_eq_norm_prev_sq_add_norm_deriv_sq`, the `CompleteSpace` instance) is a parallel API with no consumer anywhere in the repo; W2p and W3p define copies of all of it instead. Only `WeakDerivStepJetLp`, `weakDerivStepSubmodule` and the two `mem_*` lemmas are actually reused.

findings.fix: Port W2p to the step in the same PR (this file is already being edited): `W2p.firstOrderL := WeakDerivStep.prevL W1p.gradientL`, `W2p.hessianL := WeakDerivStep.derivL W1p.gradientL`, `W2p.mk := WeakDerivStep.mk W1p.gradientL`, and each lemma as a one-line application.
findings.issue: The same duplication is left in place for W2p: after w2pSubmodule is redefined as `weakDerivStepSubmodule mu Omega p W1p.gradientL` (line 70), the projections and their lemmas at lines 98-212 (firstOrderL/firstOrder/firstOrderL_apply/firstOrder_coe, hessianL/hessian/hessianL_apply/hessian_coe, W2p.mk, firstOrder_mk, hessian_mk, hasWeakFDerivOn_gradient, norm_firstOrder_le, norm_hessian_le, norm_sq_eq_norm_firstOrder_sq_add_norm_hessian_sq, the CompleteSpace instance) still re-derive `WeakDerivStep.prevL … CompleteSpace` from scratch, so nothing consumes the step API the PR added.

findings.evidence: W3p.lean:177-184 is W2p.lean:168-174 with firstOrder→secondOrder, hessian→thirdDerivative; `HasWeakFDerivOn.ae_eq` (WeakDeriv.lean:594) is stated for arbitrary `F`, and GraphStep's variable block already carries `FiniteDimensional ℝ E` and `CompleteSpace F`, so the generic form typechecks.
findings.fix: Add `WeakDerivStep.ext {u v} (hprev : prev base u = prev base v) (hderiv : deriv base u = deriv base v) : u = v` and `WeakDerivStep.ext_prev {u v} (h : prev base u = prev base v) : u = v` to GraphStep.lean (the latter via `Lp.ext ((hasWeakFDerivOn_prev base u).ae_eq (h ▸ hasWeakFDerivOn_prev base v))`), then `W3p.ext hvalue := WeakDerivStep.ext_prev (W2p.ext hvalue)` and likewise for W2p.
findings.issue: `W3p.ext` (174-184) and `W3p.ext_secondOrder` (154-162) are rename-clones of `W2p.ext` (W2p.lean:166-174) and `W2p.ext_firstOrder` (W2p.lean:151-155); the arguments (componentwise `Subtype.ext` through `WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv`, and `Lp.ext ∘ HasWeakFDerivOn.ae_eq` to upgrade equality of the previous component) are order-independent.

summary: The PR factors out the shared closed-graph step but then never uses the generic API it introduces: the whole `WeakDerivStep` namespace has no consumers, and W2p and W3p each re-define and re-prove every one of its members verbatim. Define the order-specific names in terms of the step (or delete the step's namespace) so each map and each fact has one home.
